# dsh-plugin-background-compaction
**English** · 简体中文
Zero-latency context compaction for DeepSeek Harness.

Stock compaction is **foreground**: the session hits the pressure threshold, and then you wait for
a

summarizer call while staring at a spinner. This plugin moves that work **ahead of time** — once
th

e conversation crosses a watermark it starts a speculative summary in the background, holds the
resu

lt, and when the hard threshold is reached it serves the held summary instantly instead of
calling t

hen the hard threshold is reached it serves the held summary instantly instead of
calling the model.

Measured on an identical 16-document / ~49 K-token task: the turn is frozen for **7 ms instead of
16

,095 ms**. Reproduce it yourself from `benchmark/`; the full analysis is in
BENCHMARK.md.
## Why this one

Every compaction strategy in the DSH ecosystem attacks a different thing. Here is what this one
does
that the others do not.
### 1. It removes the stall entirely — 99.96% of it

| | stock `compaction-basic` | this plugin |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| turn frozen during compaction |

**16,095 ms** | **7 ms** |
| worst single block | 16.1 s | 7 ms |

That is a factor of ~2,300. The number is not an estimate: it is `compaction/end.time −
compaction/s

tart.time` read out of the session event log, median of three runs. The base engine
writes `compacti

on/start` *before* it builds the summary input, so that interval is exactly the
time the turn is fro

tart` *before* it builds the summary input, so that interval is exactly the
time the turn is frozen.
### 2. Pruning tool output does not solve this — and the data proves it

`tool-result-pruner` is the usual first thing people enable, and it is genuinely useful. But it
prun

es the **payload**, and the payload is not the cost. With the pruner on, the stall went from
16.1 s

to 15.3 s — **a 5% improvement**, because the 15 seconds are one round trip to the model,
not the si
ze of what you send it.

This plugin does not compete with the pruner; it **runs it** before committing, so both layers
stack
. Pruning makes the compaction cheaper; background precomputation makes it invisible.
### 3. You keep a real summary, not a rule engine's output

The closest rival, `@aiwayds/dsh-dcp`, is excellent — it is a
`BasicCompactionEngine` subclass with

the same trigger and commit path, swapping the LLM summarizer
for a deterministic rule-based one. It
matches this plugin on latency (12 ms vs 7 ms — noise).
What it cannot do is **decide what mattered**. A rule-based summarizer preserves identifiers, paths,
commands and error traces verbatim; the prose connecting them, the reason a decision was made, the
half-finished line of reasoning that a later step depends on — that is model work. This plugin pays
a small token cost to keep it.
| | deterministic compaction (`dsh-dcp`) | this plugin |

| summary produced by | rules | the model |
| can compress semantics | no | yes |
| background token

cost | zero | ~2% (cache-amortised) |
| failure mode | drops meaning no rule preserves | falls back

2% (cache-amortised) |
| failure mode | drops meaning no rule preserves | falls back to foreground |
### 4. Speculation costs about 2%, not 100%
The obvious objection to "call the model twice" is that it doubles the bill. It does not:

| vs stock | delta |
| --- | ---: |

## Architecture & How it works

The plugin is a **replacement for `compaction-basic`**, not a side-car. DSH mounts exactly one
`Comp

actionEngine` as `ctx.compaction`, so a plugin that wants to influence compaction has to be
that ser

nEngine` as `ctx.compaction`, so a plugin that wants to influence compaction has to be
that service.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
| phase | what runs | user-visible latency |

| below watermark | nothing | — |
| crossing the watermark | `super.summarize()` on the pinned span

in the background | 0 ms added |
| at the threshold | optional `toolResultPruner` pass → pre-verifie
d held `SummaryResult` committed via `compactRegion()` | one event loop tick |

Everything else stays with the framework. `BasicCompactionEngine` still owns span validation,
tool-p

airing balance, `toolResultPruner` coordination, the `compaction/start` + `compaction/end`
durabilit

y markers, the shrink check (`framedSummaryTokens < shadowedTokens`), the
`SurfaceChangedError` fres
hness guard, and the surface fold.
### Why the span is pinned early

`compactRegion(start, end)` re-derives the summarization payload from immutable surface seqs
before

calling `summarize()`, so a summary computed for span `8..21` matches byte-for-byte when
the foregro

und later commits that same pinned span. `fingerprintSummarizationInput()` (SHA-256
over the system

head, shadowed messages, tool definitions, and effective summarizer target
`{ provider, model, maxTo

kens }`) is verified **before** `compactRegion()` starts: if anything
drifted, the held entry is dro

pped, the miss is booked against the circuit breaker, and the
engine delegates directly to a single
stock `super.compactIfNeeded()` pass.
## Limitations

- **A background call can be wasted.** When `toolResultPruner` rewrites the surface between
precompu

te and commit, the pinned span no longer matches, the held summary is dropped and booked
as a miss,

and a fresh one is computed. Observed in 2 of 3 benchmark runs. Correct behaviour, but
it costs one

extra background summarization.
- **Tokens are spent to buy latency.** +2.2% billed input versus sto

ck compaction in the benchmark.
On a strict pay-per-token budget a deterministic compactor such as
`

dsh-dcp` is cheaper.
- **Headless re-injection.** The headless runner re-appends the full prompt pac

kage after a
surface fold, which consumes most of the tokens a compaction just saved. Interactive se

ssions
do not do this.
- **Late speculation.** If a single step jumps past the threshold, the arming

window is skipped
and the plugin degrades to stock behaviour. It never speculates while already at

pressure.
- **One engine per context.** Because `ctx.compaction` is single-implementation, this plug

in
cannot run beside `compaction-basic`; it replaces it.
